security_privacy_cost_impact: A new LOGIN role exists on migrate-clean clusters: app_worker_login, with no stored credential (inert wherever every pg_hba line reaching it asks for one; under trust it logs in, as every role does), able to become app_worker and nothing else, and only by SET LOCAL ROLE. Measured: before SET LOCAL ROLE it reads nothing in app (42501); under app_worker it reads zero rows of every table app_worker may SELECT, because no policy names app_worker; it cannot become app_command, app_maintenance, authenticated, anon, app_authz or postgres, nor call a client command. No credential is in the repository: the migration sets none, workerCredentialLint refuses one in every fed source, rule 9 refuses one live on migrate-clean, and the test harness sets a generated per-run credential as a client-computed SCRAM verifier (plaintext only in a 0600 PGPASSFILE in a fresh temporary directory) and removes both in a finally. On the provisioned instance nothing changes (173 declared not applied); there, whoever holds postgres's credential could set the role's (RFC-2026-028 §3.3/2, A1R-3: measured locally that a CREATEROLE applier with ADMIN can). No cost impact.
migration_and_data_impact: One forward migration, 173_worker_login_identity.sql: one role, one membership, a comment, one apply-time block; no table, column, policy, grant on any relation or data change. No earlier apply-time block superseded. The snapshot declares 173 not applied. No open_blockers line moves ([201] is added at the end).
